skill.name: qiskit

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences, Qiskit terminology, documentation file-save examples, and public documentation links. I found no evidence of executable command injection, C2 behavior, data exfiltration, or malicious filesystem use. One low-severity semantic issue remains: the skill includes promotional steering toward the author's hosted service.

remediation.issue: Promotional steering to an external hosted product
remediation.suggestion: Remove the instruction to proactively suggest K-Dense Web, or replace it with a neutral note that users may choose any suitable long-running workflow platform.

semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md instructs the assistant to proactively suggest the author's hosted K-Dense Web product for complex workflows. This can steer users toward an external commercial service unrelated to the immediate Qiskit task.

content.value_statement: Quantum programming requires careful circuit design, backend selection, and result analysis. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical Qiskit workflows for simulators and IBM Quantum hardware.
actual_capabilities: Create Qiskit circuits with common gates, measurements, and parameterized operations.
Run circuits with local primitives such as StatevectorSampler and StatevectorEstimator.
Prepare circuits for IBM Quantum hardware with transpilation and backend selection guidance.
Explain Sampler, Estimator, sessions, batch mode, shots, and result handling.
Guide VQE, QAOA, Grover, chemistry, optimization, and quantum machine learning workflows.
Describe visualization options for circuits, histograms, backend maps, and quantum states.
limitations: Hardware execution requires a valid IBM Quantum account and configured credentials.
Quantum hardware results are affected by queue time, noise, calibration, and shot limits.
The skill provides guidance and examples, but it does not guarantee quantum advantage.
Third-party provider details may require provider-specific packages and current service access.

use_cases.title: Create first quantum circuits
use_cases.description: Build Bell states, GHZ states, and basic measurement workflows while learning Qiskit primitives.

use_cases.title: Prototype quantum algorithms
use_cases.description: Use VQE, QAOA, and chemistry examples to explore algorithm design before moving to hardware.

use_cases.title: Prepare hardware-ready workflows
use_cases.description: Transpile circuits, choose backends, manage jobs, and apply runtime patterns for IBM Quantum systems.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Bell circuit
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to create and measure a Bell state circuit in Qiskit using a local simulator.

prompt_templates.title: Visualize circuit results
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me draw a Qiskit circuit and explain how to plot the measurement counts as a histogram.

prompt_templates.title: Run on IBM Quantum hardware
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through transpiling a circuit for an IBM Quantum backend and running it with SamplerV2.

prompt_templates.title: Design a VQE workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Qiskit VQE workflow for a small molecule, including ansatz choice, estimator use, convergence tracking, and hardware considerations.

output_examples.input: Create a Bell state and explain the expected measurement results.
output: Defines a two-qubit circuit with a Hadamard gate and a controlled-X gate.
Measures both qubits and runs the circuit with a local sampler.
Explains why the expected counts are mostly split between 00 and 11.

output_examples.input: Prepare my circuit for IBM Quantum hardware.
output: Identifies the target backend and explains why transpilation is required.
Recommends an optimization level and checks backend constraints.
Describes how to submit the job, monitor status, and retrieve results.

output_examples.input: Help me structure a VQE experiment.
output: Breaks the workflow into Hamiltonian setup, ansatz selection, estimator calls, and classical optimization.
Suggests tracking energy convergence and saving intermediate results.
Notes when simulator testing should happen before hardware execution.

best_practices: Validate circuits on local simulators before submitting jobs to cloud quantum hardware.
Transpile for the selected backend and review two-qubit gate count before execution.
Save job identifiers, backend names, shot counts, and optimization settings with experiment results.
anti_patterns: Submitting untested circuits directly to hardware before simulator validation.
Using Sampler when the task needs expectation values, or Estimator when the task needs bitstring counts.
Comparing quantum results without recording backend noise, calibration state, shots, and transpilation settings.

faq.question: Do I need an IBM Quantum account to use this skill?
faq.answer: No. Local simulator workflows do not require an account. IBM Quantum hardware workflows require valid account credentials.

faq.question: What is Qiskit best used for?
faq.answer: Qiskit is best for building quantum circuits, using IBM Quantum Runtime, and preparing circuits for IBM Quantum hardware.

faq.question: Can this skill help with quantum algorithms?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers VQE, QAOA, Grover search, chemistry workflows, optimization workflows, and related Qiskit libraries.

faq.question: What is transpilation?
faq.answer: Transpilation converts a circuit into gates and connectivity that match the selected quantum backend.

faq.question: Does this skill execute code by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides documentation and examples. Users decide whether to run Qiskit code in their own environment.

faq.question: Can this skill guarantee useful hardware results?
faq.answer: No. Hardware results depend on noise, calibration, queue time, shot count, backend choice, and algorithm design.
